**EthnoBotaPhyWR** stands for *ethnobotany*, *phytochemistry*, *Wikidata* and
*R* [(maybe you can also find the *bot* of *robot*)]{.smallcaps} It should be
pronounced "Ethnobota Fever".

```{r}
#| label: imports
#| include: false

## External sources
source(
  file = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adafede/cascade/main/R/colors.R"
)
library(EthnoBotaPhyWR)
```

## Introduction

This vignette illustrates how to collect data on the *ethnobotanical uses*, and
the *phytochemistry* of a given taxonomic family. The data collected originate
from [Wikidata](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Main_Page), the free
knowledge base that anyone can edit.

At the moment, this vignette supports adding your own data and combine them with
the ones available on Wikidata to see the results. Ideally, you should share
these precious data.

### tl;dr

The function you are looking for is `ethnobotafever_tree()`, whose parameters
are described below:

```{r}
#| label: parameters

## Taxonomy-related parameters
taxon_name <- "Orchidaceae" # The scientific name of the family you are interested in

example_family_names <- list( # The scientific name(s) of family(ies) you want to compare to
  "Poaceae" = "Poaceae",
  "Fabaceae" = "Fabaceae",
  "Asteraceae" = "Asteraceae",
  "Orchidaceae" = "Orchidaceae",
  "Rosaceae" = "Rosaceae",
  "Solanaceae" = "Solanaceae"
)

## Thresholds
n_multiple_genera <- 10L # The minimal number of genera where a compound was found in to consider the latter relatively widespread
n_ethnobotanical_count_min <- 10L # The minimal number of species within the genus for which an ethnobotanical use has been reported to consider the genus relatively widely used
n_compounds_count_min <- 50L # The minimal number of compounds reported in a taxon to consider the latter relatively widely investigated

## File paths
path_molecules <- "~/Documents/papers/orchids/orchids_table_unique_connectivity_classified.tsv"
path_classes <- "~/Documents/papers/orchids/orchids_compounds_classes.tsv"
path_ethnobotanical <- "~/Documents/papers/orchids/Species_medicinal_output_with_ott_id.tsv"

export_tree_full <- "man/figures/tree_orchids_full.pdf"
export_tree_phyto <- "man/figures/tree_orchids_phyto.pdf"
export_tree_phyto_sub <- "man/figures/tree_orchids_phyto_sub.pdf"
export_table_classified <- "~/Documents/papers/orchids/orchids_table_unique_connectivity_classified.tsv"
export_table_counts <- "~/Documents/papers/orchids/orchids_table_counts.tsv"
export_table_counts_sub <- "~/Documents/papers/orchids/orchids_table_counts_sub.tsv"

local_cache <- ".cache/"
log_dir <- "~/Documents/papers/orchids/"
```

Change these parameters as required and you are ready for the fever!

```{r}
#| label: ethnobotafever_tree
#| message: false
#| warning: false

results <- ethnobotafever_tree(
  taxon_name = taxon_name,
  n_multiple_genera = n_multiple_genera,
  n_ethnobotanical_count_min = n_ethnobotanical_count_min,
  n_compounds_count_min = n_compounds_count_min,
  example_family_names = example_family_names,
  path_molecules = path_molecules,
  path_classes = path_classes,
  path_ethnobotanical = path_ethnobotanical,
  export_tree_full = export_tree_full,
  export_tree_phyto = export_tree_phyto,
  export_tree_phyto_sub = export_tree_phyto_sub,
  export_table_classified = export_table_classified,
  export_table_counts = export_table_counts,
  export_table_counts_sub = export_table_counts_sub,
  local_cache = local_cache,
  log_dir = log_dir
)
```

## Results {#sec-results}

This will give you different objets

First, tables containing different information:

- An overview of the phytochemistry of the family in @tbl-1
- An overview of the number of reported uses, compounds, and species per genus
  within the family in @tbl-2
- An overview of the species within the family for which a decent number of
  compounds or uses have been reported in @tbl-3

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-1
#| tbl-cap: "Overview of the phytochemistry of the family"

results$df_taxa_full |>
  data.frame() |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::opt_interactive()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-2
#| tbl-cap: "Overview of the number of reported uses, compounds, and species per genus within the family"

results$df_taxa_ethno_counted |>
  data.frame() |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::opt_interactive()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-3
#| tbl-cap: "Overview of the species within the family for which a decent number of compounds or uses have been reported"

results$df_taxa_known_sub |>
  data.frame() |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::opt_interactive()
```

Second, some tree-based visualizations:

- A tree with genera as tips, displaying the taxa of the family, and if
  compounds or uses have been reported in @fig-1 (mainly to show the majority
  remains non-investigated)
- A tree with genera as tips, displaying the taxa of the family for which
  compounds or uses have been reported in @fig-2 (mainly to make them easier to
  read)
- A tree with species as tips, displaying the taxa of the family for which a
  decent number of compounds or uses have been reported in the corresponding
  genus in @fig-3 (mainly to show that even in the most investigated genera, the
  coverage is far from ideal)

![A tree with genera as tips, displaying the taxa of the family, and if compounds or uses have been reported](man/figures/tree_orchids_full.pdf){#fig-1 width=100%}

![A tree with genera as tips, displaying the taxa of the family for which compounds or uses have been reported](man/figures/tree_orchids_phyto.pdf){#fig-2 width=100%}

![A tree with species as tips, displaying the taxa of the family for which a decent number of compounds or uses have been reported in the corresponding genus](man/figures/tree_orchids_phyto_sub.pdf){#fig-3 width=100%}
